terra.problem: Saying Jeremiah cannot find any spot without suffering goes beyond the country and city described in the verse.
Saying nobody is picking up a trowel asserts more than the verse says.
“Nobody gets skipped” extends the statement beyond the prophet and priest named in the verse.
The prayer does point to something they have done: it acknowledges that they have sinned.
The descriptions of Moses as Israel’s leader and Samuel as a prophet need references because those facts are outside the passage.
Saying the disgrace and humiliation come after the mother breathes her last presents the verse’s sequence as the order of events, which the text does not establish.
